attempts.summary: On node1 (RHEL 9.8), configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3 so new user passwords must be at least 12 characters and use at least 3 distinct character classes. PAM already invoked pam_pwquality.so via authselect's system-auth/password-auth (requisite), so no PAM stack changes were needed. Verified enforcement as a non-root user (root bypasses pwquality by default, so tests were run via sudo -u testuser passwd): a sub-12-char password was rejected, a 12+ char password with only 2 classes was rejected, and a 12+ char 3-class password was accepted. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and config state, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified the pwquality config, PAM hooks, and live password enforcement post-reboot with a fresh test user, then cleaned up all test users.
